name: Customer segments
prompt: Compare customer segments: revenue and orders by segment, segment KPIs, and a segment detail table.

binding.sql: SELECT SUM(customers) AS customers FROM customer_segments
SELECT ROUND(SUM(revenue),0) AS revenue FROM customer_segments
SELECT segment AS segment, ROUND(SUM(revenue),0) AS revenue FROM customer_segments GROUP BY segment ORDER BY revenue DESC

copy.title: Revenue by segment
copy.caption: Pro accounts generate $1.44M — four times the business segment — despite equal customer counts.

binding.sql: SELECT segment AS segment, SUM(orders) AS orders FROM customer_segments GROUP BY segment ORDER BY orders DESC

copy.title: Orders by segment
copy.caption: Order counts are nearly identical across segments — the gap is in order value, not frequency.

binding.sql: SELECT segment AS segment, SUM(customers) AS customers, SUM(orders) AS orders, ROUND(SUM(revenue),0) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(revenue)/NULLIF(SUM(orders),0),0) AS avg_order_value FROM customer_segments GROUP BY segment ORDER BY revenue DESC

copy.title: Segment detail
copy.caption: Pro and consumer segments lead on value per order; business trails at $279.
